whatLandedAgainstTheDispatchItems.item2_logicalEdgeGrouping: groupRingChordsIntoLogicalEdges: a maximal run of consecutive chords whose turn at each shared vertex is <= 10.0 degrees is ONE logical edge carrying its chord indices, length and bearing. tolerancesChosenAndWhy.theMeasuredBandThatSetsThem: Turn at every vertex of all four real fixture rings, sorted, is in CP1's header and in ring-logical-edges.test.ts: the largest turn that belongs to a DIGITISED line is 0.03 degrees (48209:97658's three collinear runs), the largest turn that belongs to a frontage CURVE is 11.17 degrees, and the shallowest real corner is 70.16 degrees. 10 degrees sits between the curve and the corner on purpose: it keeps a curve OUT of the line groups (fusing 9.15-11.17 degrees would report a curve as straight, which is a lie) and the curve is then handled as a frontage RUN by 45 degrees instead, whose own margin is 32.1 degrees inside the run and 57.2 at its nearest end.
tolerancesChosenAndWhy.nonArbitrarinessMeasured: F4: no value in the scrub range 0.1-1.0 m nor the grouping range 2-45 degrees changes either real fixture's answer, swept in ring-logical-edges.test.ts; the only thresholds that DO change it are ones that also merge a real 90-degree corner.

contradicted.what: MY OWN CP1 PREDICTION under F1: 'the envelope is non-zero and passing P1-P3, ~1,478 sq ft by arithmetic from the role set'.
contradicted.measured: 5018.6 sq ft (6 vertices), P1/P2/P3 all pass. My arithmetic was wrong, not the envelope: I applied the 25 ft front and 20 ft rear setbacks ACROSS the 16.80 m axis, but e2 (the frontage, 16.80 m = 55 ft) is the line the setbacks measure FROM — the lot is 55 ft wide and 156 ft DEEP, so the buildable depth is 47.6 - 7.62 - 6.10 = 33.9 m and the buildable width is 16.8 - 2 x 1.52 = 13.76 m, giving 466 sq m = 5,018 sq ft (58% of the 8,615 sq ft lot, which is what a deep narrow lot gives under 25/5/20). The measurement is the correct one and the pre-registration is recorded as wrong.

contradicted.what: MY OWN CP1 PREDICTION for the synthetic artifact ring: 'the envelope is non-zero and IDENTICAL to the clean rectangle's'.
contradicted.measured: FALSE, and pinned as false. Labels and verdicts ARE artifact-invariant (the scrub recovers the clean ring's own four corners to within 1e-12 degrees; every gate passes on both rings; one front line and one rear line), but the DRAWN boundary is not: the 0.05 m bump survives the offset core, which miters at the bump — 7 boundary vertices against the clean control's 5, and area 2434.1 sq ft against 2499.4 (2.6% smaller, positions within ~0.15 m). Recorded rather than smoothed over: it is a leave-behind of the same family as the R32 residual, and the test states the numbers so a future fix has to change them deliberately.

contradicted.what: THE DISPATCH'S DEFECT SENTENCE: 'Its front is inferred from the nearest street centerline instead of the situs-named street.' (carried from CP1, still standing after implementation)
contradicted.measured: FALSE on the live ring, and unchanged by this lane: with named roads present the R30 situs path already matched ('629 STURGEON DR' -> STURGEON, OSM 'Sturgeon Street' -> STURGEON) and already picked the closest Sturgeon edge at 7.6 m, which is also the nearest street. The reproducible pre-fix failures are the artifact-chord ROLES and the resulting false zero, not the front's basis. The dispatch's '609 Sturgeon Dr' is also wrong: the county service and the ledger-truth rail both read 629.

contradicted.what: THE DISPATCH'S PREMISE: 'LDT's live labeller does group ring chords into logical edges.' (carried from CP1)
contradicted.measured: FALSE as stated: LDT does not group chords. It avoids this failure by a different route (it excludes sub-survey slivers from front candidacy and REFUSES a shape whose front is ambiguous). The deliverable is unchanged because the engine side genuinely lacked the grouping and needed it — but the divergence test's declared differences are generated from what LDT ACTUALLY does, not from that sentence.

Pinned in p262-fixture-gate.test.ts with the exact reason string, and the test says explicitly which assertions flip when the offset core learns a curve.
